summary: A 1931 cupola cabin in Clearwater County, abandoned in 1961 and listed as gone; sources say little else.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1961 and recorded as gone.

events.note: One known staff member named on the Idaho Fire Lookouts site (Bill Bailey); single source, not confirmed

evidence.supports: built 1931 as a cupola cabin; abandoned 1961; gone
11 miles east of what the page calls Headquarters
both pages carry the initials CTPA
Elk Butte page names the Clearwater-Potlatch Timber Protective Association
one known staff member, Bill Bailey, at the Columbia Breaks Fire Center

notes_for_editor: Both East Elk pages are hobby-site entries, and the Idaho site appears to repeat firelookout.com's dates, so there is one line of evidence, not two. The 1933 staff entry (Bill Bailey, Columbia Breaks Fire Center) appears on the Idaho page only and no second source was found; it is in the story with that caveat, and an editor may prefer to cut it. The CTPA label appears on both East Elk pages in the place Dog Point's page gives its Forest Service, so it is read as the agency; the expansion comes from the Elk Butte page and is probably the same body, not confirmed for East Elk. The 1957-58 association report (objects.lib.uidaho.edu/tpa/pot_tpa1957-1958.pdf) names Elk Butte, Mason Butte, Stockton Meadows and Freezeout as the four lookouts manned in 1957 and does not mention East Elk. No Forest Service record, photo or site description was found. Access, current ownership and what remains on the site are unknown. A search also surfaced Elk Butte and Elk Summit, which are different lookouts and are not used here.
